tax_brackets_note: IRAS resident individual income tax rates from YA 2024 onwards (Budget 2023 revised). Source: https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/tax-residency-and-tax-rates/individual-income-tax-rates

thresholds.filing_threshold_note: IRAS filing obligation applies when annual income exceeds $22,000. The threshold of 0 here means all staking/reward income is included in the calculation with no pre-filter; the $20,000 tax-free bracket in the progressive table handles the de minimis effect.

rates.capital_gain_note: Singapore does not impose capital gains tax. Gains from disposal of digital tokens held as investments are not taxable.

trader_assessment.description: IRAS e-Tax Guide: Income Tax Treatment of Digital Tokens (2020). Badges of trade indicators to distinguish capital gains (not taxable) from trading income (taxable).
trader_assessment.classification_note: If badges of trade indicate trading activity, gains are taxable as income under ITA s.10(1)(a). Otherwise treated as capital gains (not taxable).

references.excerpt: Resident individual tax rates from YA 2024: 0% up to $20,000; progressive rates up to 24% above $1,000,000.

notes: Classify staking/lending/jumpstart as potential taxable income
Capital gains from investment-purpose disposal are NOT taxable
Trader vs investor classification uses IRAS badges of trade framework
Tax brackets apply only to taxable income (staking/trading income), not capital gains

OKX Jumpstart rewards: treated similarly to staking rewards — tokens received for participating are classified as income at fair market value upon receipt (per IRAS e-Tax Guide s.3 on mining/staking rewards analogy)
